# Memory — Standing Instructions

> These instructions are enforced across all skill and agent invocations.
> Memory is the **authoritative source** for coding standards, architecture, testing, logging, and security.
> Plans may contain plan-specific overrides but should not duplicate these rules.
> Managed by the Memorize skill. Do not edit section headers manually.
> To add or change instructions, invoke: `/memorize <your instructions>`
> To override: `/memorize override <your instructions>`
> To generate from project analysis: `/memorize bootstrap`

## General

- Look at the big picture: avoid churning out similar code in multiple places. Abstract shared logic into common utility or helper methods. When changing functionality or features, if backwards-compatibility expectations are not already explicit in memory or the request, ask the user whether backwards compatibility is required before proceeding. If backwards compatibility is **not** required, do not preserve deprecated signatures, unused parameters, or legacy behavior — remove them cleanly.
- Yantra is a **browser-automation platform**, not a general AI agent. Reject scope creep into desktop automation, code generation, file management, or non-browser tasks — the tool catalog is intentionally narrow.
- Honesty over cleverness: when sites block legitimate automation (bot detection, CAPTCHA, 429), we honor the block and hand off to the user. We never escalate, evade, or fingerprint-cloak.
- **Local-first by default.** No telemetry to external services. The run directory is the durable artifact; users own their data.

## Tech Stack

- **Language**: TypeScript 5+, strict mode (`"strict": true` in `tsconfig.json`).
- **Runtime**: Node 24.15.0 LTS. ESM-only — no CommonJS fallbacks.
- **Monorepo tooling**: pnpm workspaces + Turborepo (selective rebuilds, shared CI cache).
- **Browser driver**: `puppeteer-core` with CDP pipe transport (`--remote-debugging-pipe`). System Chrome only in MVP; bundled Chromium via `@puppeteer/browsers` is a Phase 2 add-on.
- **LLM client**: `pi-agent-core` ([earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/agent/README.md)) — wrapped behind an internal `LLMClient` interface in `packages/agent`. Default provider: Anthropic; second supported: Ollama. OpenAI in Phase 2.
- **Schemas**: `zod` (source of truth) + `zod-to-json-schema` (JSON Schema emission) + custom adapter to pi-agent-core tool definitions.
- **Workflow expressions**: `jsonata` — sandboxed, no custom functions, expression timeout enforced.
- **Content extraction**: `@mozilla/readability` + `cheerio`.
- **YAML parser**: `yaml` (eemeli — better spec compliance than js-yaml).
- **Keychain**: `keytar` (deprecation by Microsoft tracked as Phase 2 migration risk).
- **Logging**: `pino` (structured JSON).
- **Testing**: `vitest` (unit + integration) + `fast-check` (property tests) + Playwright (end-to-end of our own CLI).
- **CLI framework**: `commander`.
- **Search fast-path (optional)**: Tavily or Brave Search API, with graceful browser-driven fallback.
- When adding new packages, strictly fetch the **latest stable** (not pre-release) versions. Strongly prefer Long Term Support (LTS) distributions for all libraries, frameworks, and runtimes.

## Project Structure

- **4 packages + 1 app**:
  - `packages/protocol/` — Zod schemas → JSON Schema → TS types → pi-agent-core tool defs. Zero runtime deps beyond zod.
  - `packages/core/` — browser, locator, executor, extraction, sanitizer, secrets, workflow, ethics, audit, events. Folder-level internal seams.
  - `packages/agent/` — pi-agent-core adapter. **Forbidden to import from `core`** — compiler-enforced.
  - `apps/cli/` — commander-based entrypoint; runs executor inline. Internal IO abstraction is the future Connector seam.
  - `e2e/` — cross-package end-to-end tests (golden traces, chaos suite, recorder/replay round-trip).
  - `docs/` — generated protocol spec, getting-started, workflow YAML reference.
- **File naming**: `kebab-case.ts` for files; `PascalCase.ts` only for files that export a single class.
- **Test files**: keep tests in dedicated test directories (for example `tests/`), mirrored to source structure. Do not mix test files into source directories.
- Keep long-form project documentation in the root `docs/` directory only (outside `packages/`), unless the user explicitly requests an exception.
- **Persistence is filesystem-based**, not relational:
  - Workflows: `~/.local/share/yantra/workflows/<name>.yaml` (+ optional `<name>.locators.json` sidecar)
  - Runs: `~/.local/share/yantra/runs/<run-id>/` (manifest.json, plan.json, agent.jsonl, secrets.jsonl, events.jsonl, checkpoints/, outputs.json, report.md)
  - Profiles: per-workflow Chrome user-data-dir under `~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/<workflow>/`
  - Secrets: OS keychain only — never on disk
  - Config: `~/.config/yantra/config.yaml`

## Coding Standards

- **TypeScript strict everywhere.** No `any` in `packages/protocol` or `packages/agent` (trust-boundary packages). Elsewhere, `any` requires a justification comment. Use `unknown` + type narrowing when typing is genuinely open.
- **Naming**: `camelCase` for variables/functions, `PascalCase` for classes/interfaces/types/enums, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. No `I` prefix on interfaces.
- Prefer `interface` over `type` for object shapes that may be extended. Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types.
- Use `readonly` and `const` by default. Mutate only with clear reason.
- Prefer **named exports** over default exports.
- Use `enum` sparingly — prefer `const` objects with `as const` or union types.
- **`null` is preferred in `packages/protocol` types** (JSON Schema interop — `null` round-trips, `undefined` does not). Elsewhere, `undefined` is preferred for absence. Be consistent within each package.
- Use `async`/`await` over raw Promises. Never mix callbacks with Promises. No floating promises — always `await` or explicitly handle.
- Custom error classes extend `Error` and carry context (what failed, why, with what input).

## Architecture

- Follow **SOLID** principles (Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion) and clean-code principles. **Prefer composition over multi-level inheritance.** Use interfaces to decouple components.
- **Layered architecture**: `protocol` is the shared contract; `core` and `agent` consume `protocol`; `apps/cli` consumes everything. `agent` cannot import `core` — compiler-enforced.
- **Yantra Protocol is the single source of truth** for the agent/engine contract. Touching a step verb's signature is one edit in `packages/protocol`; TS types, JSON Schema, and pi-agent-core tool defs regenerate atomically.
- **Plans are finite, not loops.** The agent emits a complete, validated `Plan.steps` array up front. No ReAct mid-execution in MVP. Branching is explicit via `BranchStep`; iteration via `LoopStep` over a known collection.
- **Two-stage plan validation** before any browser action: (1) schema validation via Zod; (2) semantic validation (CaptureRef resolution, SecretRef declaration check, locator name resolution, contextual-scope rules). Validation errors trigger bounded re-prompt (max 2 retries) for agent-produced plans, then abort with structured report.
- **Single sanitizer chokepoint** for every LLM-bound payload. Direct `pi-agent-core` invocations outside `packages/agent` are forbidden.
- **Candidate-chain resolution is the engine's responsibility, never the agent's.** The agent never emits CSS/XPath/role expressions in MVP. LLM reanchor is Phase 2 with element-uniqueness validation.
- **Dependency Injection** via constructor or function parameters. Avoid module-level singletons that are hard to test. No DI framework — explicit constructor params are fine for this size.

## Design Patterns

- **Schema-as-source-of-truth** (Zod) — single Zod schema produces TS types, JSON Schema, and tool definitions.
- **Adapter pattern** wrapping `pi-agent-core` behind the internal `LLMClient` interface — isolates provider-API churn and serves as the sanitizer enforcement seam.
- **Strategy pattern** for pluggable providers: `BrowserProvider`, `LLMClient`, `SearchProvider`, `KeychainProvider`.
- **Repository-like abstractions** for persistence boundaries: `WorkflowStore`, `RunStore`, `SecretStore` — abstract storage behind interfaces, easy to mock in tests.
- **DTOs at boundaries**: Zod schemas validate all external input (CLI args, workflow YAML, LLM responses, captured DOM payloads).
- **Discriminated unions** for closed enumerations (`Step`, `TaskEvent`, `ValueRef`, `LocatorChain`) — preferred over class hierarchies.
- **Result Pattern**: All fallible operations return `Result<T, E>` — `{ isOk: true, value: T }` for success, `{ isOk: false, error: E }` for failure. Use `ok()` and `err()` helpers from `utils/result.ts`.
- **Custom Hook Extraction**: Extract all non-trivial component logic into custom hooks (`use<Domain>.ts`) (for react app)

## Error Handling

- All fallible adapter calls must use the `Result<T, E>` pattern. Never use bare `try/catch` around adapter calls.
- Check `result.isOk` before accessing `result.value`. Always handle the error branch.
- Use centralized error handling per layer. Never `catch` generic `Error` and silently swallow. At minimum, log and re-throw.
- **Custom error classes** extending `Error` for domain-specific failures (`PlanValidationError`, `LocatorNotFoundError`, `EthicsRefusedError`, `SecretNotFoundError`, `ScopeViolationError`, `LLMUnavailableError`).
- **Bounded re-prompt** on agent plan validation failure: max 2 retries with structured error context, then abort with `report.md`.
- **Every run-aborting failure** emits a `task_failed` event paired with a `report.md` in the run directory. No silent failures, no `process.exit(0)` on error.
- **Exit codes**: `0` success; `1` validation error (bad YAML, missing flag); `2` execution failure (run started, ended in failure); `3` environment failure (`doctor` issue); `4` user-handoff abort (CAPTCHA, MFA without seed).
- **`LLMUnavailable` is a typed error**, not a silent degradation. When `LLM_PROVIDER=none`, callers either fall through to a deterministic alternative (the `ask` rule-based path) or return `LLMUnavailable` for the caller to render as an actionable message.

## Logging

- Implement **structured JSON logging** with `pino`. Never use `console.log` in production code paths.
- Log levels mapped to Yantra concepts: `error` = run-aborting failure (paired with `task_failed` event); `warn` = recoverable issue (retry, fallback); `info` = task-level events; `debug` = step-level, locator-candidate, sanitizer transformations.
- **Never log secrets, tokens, passwords, credentials, or PII.** Pino is configured with a secret-shape redactor as defense-in-depth; the primary guarantee is "we never log secrets" via the resolver and reviewer discipline.
- **The run directory is the canonical observability artifact** (`events.jsonl`, `agent.jsonl`, `secrets.jsonl`, `report.md`). No telemetry to external services. Pino dual-writes to the run dir and (when `--debug`) the executor's stdout.
- **TaskEvent stream is the source of truth** for state transitions; logs are commentary. Tests inspect events, not log output.
- **Mandatory audit events**:
  - Every `LLMClient.send` → `agent.jsonl` entry with `{prompt_sanitized, response, model, latency_ms, cost_usd, ts}`
  - Every secret resolution → `secrets.jsonl` entry with `{key, step_id, ts}` (no value)
  - Every plan validation failure → `events.jsonl` with offending path
  - Every contextual-scope violation → `events.jsonl` with `{scope, attempted_verb, step_id}` plus run abort
  - Every robots.txt or blocklist refusal → `events.jsonl` with `{host, rule, reason}`

## Testing

- Follow test-naming best practices: describe behavior, not method names (`it('returns a structured failure report when all locator candidates exhaust')` over `it('test runLocator')`).
- **Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA)** pattern in every test.
- Mock external dependencies (network, filesystem at boundaries, keychain, LLM provider) — never mock internal business logic.
- Use factories or builders for test data — avoid hardcoded fixtures that become brittle.
- **Property-based tests are non-optional for**: (1) the sanitizer in `packages/core/sanitizer` — generate diverse payloads; assert no credential-shaped string ever appears in output; (2) the protocol validator in `packages/protocol` — generate malformed plans; assert validation returns either a valid plan or an actionable error, never panics; (3) the contextual-scope enforcer in `packages/core/secrets` — generate mixed-scope plans; assert read-only-data scope rejects mutating verbs 100% of the time.
- **CI matrix**: macOS + Windows + Ubuntu × `LLM_PROVIDER ∈ {anthropic, none}` from day one. Tests tagged `@no-llm` run in both modes and must pass in both; `@requires-llm` skipped in `none` mode; spine tests are mandatorily `@no-llm`.
- **End-to-end** suites in `e2e/`: golden-plan suite (canonical intents → canonical plans, pinned per LLM model); chaos suite (inject each failure class; assert clean termination + structured report 100% of runs); recorder/replay round-trip suite.
- If existing tests are already failing, do not assume the implementation is wrong — explicitly ask the user whether to fix tests, fix code, or proceed with scoped changes.
- Aim for high coverage on business logic and critical paths (sanitizer, protocol validator, scope enforcer, executor, locator engine). Don't chase 100% on glue code.

## Security

- **Three structural guarantees**, each enforced by a distinct mechanism:
  1. **Agent never sees literal secrets** — `ValueRef` discriminated union + worker resolves at execution boundary + CI static-analysis grep on every `LLMClient.send` call.
  2. **Agent never sees unsanitized authenticated content** — single sanitizer chokepoint with per-class profiles + property-based tests on realistic corpora.
  3. **User can audit what the agent saw and did** — every LLM call and secret resolution logged to the run directory; `yantra audit <run-id>` renders the trail.
- **Contextual scopes** (`public` / `read-only-data` / `authenticated`) declared per step in workflow YAML. The `read-only-data` scope statically rejects mutating step verbs (`click`, `fill`, `navigate` to a new host, side-effect `assert`) — the executor enforces this before any browser instantiation. Property-based tests assert the rejection is 100%.
- **Secrets live only in the OS keychain.** Never written to disk in plan files, run logs, checkpoints, or event streams. Event streams emit `{kind:"secret", key}` references; clients render them as `••••• (key)`. `Buffer.fill(0)` on secret strings post-use (best-effort mitigation in Node).
- **Validate all external input at the boundary** with Zod schemas: CLI args, workflow YAML, LLM responses, captured DOM payloads.
- **No literal credentials in workflow YAML.** `yantra lint` warns + `yantra run` errors if a `value:` field contains a string matching common credential shapes (sk-, ghp\_, AKIA, eyJ…).
- **CDP-pipe transport, not WebSocket port** — eliminates localhost-port attack surface in puppeteer-core.
- **Ethics gate is non-bypassable** in MVP: robots.txt, blocklist, and per-host rate limit checks live in the executor before any navigate/click. No `--ignore-robots` flag.
- **Search-API keys** live in the OS keychain (`tavily.api_key`, `brave.api_key`) — referenced by config, never stored in `config.yaml`.
- `yantra doctor` warns if `~/.local/share/yantra/` has world-readable permissions.
- Threat-model boundaries documented in plan §6. Out of scope: compromised local machine, side-channel timing attacks, HSM-backed keys.

## Dependencies

- **Latest stable (not pre-release) versions.** Strongly prefer LTS distributions for libraries, frameworks, and runtimes.
- Pin major versions in `package.json`. Run `npm audit` (or `pnpm audit`) in CI.
- **Two LLM providers from day one** (Anthropic + Ollama via pi-agent-core) — exposes provider drift early and avoids vendor lock-in for a privacy-sensitive tool.
- **Direct `pi-agent-core` invocations outside `packages/agent` are forbidden** — enforced by import-restriction lint rule. The `LLMClient` interface is the only authorized entry point.
- Track `keytar` deprecation (Microsoft has deprecated it) — migration to `node-keychain` or Tauri keyring is a Phase 2 task in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`.
- Before installing a specific version of a new dependency, check with the user.

## Documentation

- Every public method or function must include clear, human-readable comments that describe its purpose, parameters, return value, and any side effects. Comments are written for a broad audience — not just the original author.
- All public APIs (exports from `packages/*`) require JSDoc with `@param`, `@returns`, and `@example` where appropriate.
- Maintain a single canonical `README.md` at the repository root. Do not add additional README files in subdirectories unless the user explicitly requests one.
- **Zod schemas in `packages/protocol` use inline `.describe()` calls** — these feed the auto-generated protocol spec page in `docs/` and the agent's system-prompt tool catalog.
- Workflow YAML files are human-readable by design: step verbs read like English (`navigate`, `fill`, `click`, `extract`, `wait_for`). Raw CSS at step level is a lint warning. A non-author should be able to scan a workflow in 30 seconds and understand what it does.
- Generated artifacts (`docs/protocol-spec.md`, getting-started, workflow YAML reference) are produced from schemas + `.describe()` annotations + curated guidance — not hand-maintained.
